name: Hochzeiger Bergbahnen
kurzbeschreibung: The Hochzeiger Bergbahnen in the Pitztal valley impress up to 2,500 m altitude with the ZirbenPark, a 12 m adventure tower, and thrilling ZirbenCarts.
preis: Gondel Berg- und Talfahrt Erwachsene 29,00 €, Kinder 13,00 €; ZirbenPark Eintritt frei
oeffnungszeiten: Anfang Juni bis Mitte Okt täglich 09:00–17:00 Uhr (Winter Dez–Apr)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Hochzeiger Bergbahnen provide access to the popular hiking and skiing area surrounding the 2,560-metre-high Hochzeiger above Jerzens in the front Pitztal. From the valley station at an altitude of 1,450 metres, modern cable car facilities ascend to snow-reliable heights of 2,500 metres. Surrounded by one of Northern Tyrol's largest contiguous stone pine forests, the area has established itself under the banner of the "Queen of the Alps" as a multifaceted nature and adventure mountain. Unique attractions such as the ZirbenPark, the monumental ZirbenZapfen tower, and fast-paced ZirbenCarts make the area an outstanding excursion destination for families and alpine hikers.

ZirbenPark & Fun Sports Attractions

At the centre of the summer offerings at the middle station at 2,000 metres above sea level lies the approximately one-kilometre-long ZirbenPark-Erlebnisweg: on an easily accessible circular trail, visitors learn fascinating facts about the Swiss stone pine (Zirbe), its essential oils, and its soothing effects on the human cardiovascular system across interactive sensory and activity stations. The unmistakable landmark is the 12-metre-high ZirbenZapfen: a wooden adventure tower with a viewing platform offering sweeping views across the Pitztal, which can be exited via a rapid 16-metre-long tube slide. The park is complemented by a giant wooden marble run, a stone pine water labyrinth, and the popular Zirbennest relaxation spot. Adrenaline rushes are guaranteed by the ZirbenCarts: from the mountain station of the Hochzeiger 2.5 chairlift, fun sports enthusiasts steer three-wheeled downhill mountain carts across an almost four-kilometre-long, curving natural track with a descent of around 500 vertical metres down to the middle station.

Visit & Getting There

The Hochzeiger Bergbahnen operate during the summer season from early June to mid-October daily from 09:00 to 17:00. Admission to the ZirbenPark is free – guests only require a cable car ticket to the middle station. Summer 2025/2026 tariffs: round-trip gondola ascent and descent to the middle station €29.00 for adults, €13.00 for children; day ticket for all cable cars €39.00 for adults, €19.00 for children. ZirbenCart ride including lift transport: €15.00 per ride (minimum age 12 years and 150 cm height; younger children ride together with an adult). Holders of the regional Pitztal Sommer Card use the cable cars free of charge! Travel by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 to Imst/Pitztal, on the Pitztaler Landesstraße L16 via Wenns to Jerzens and onward to the Hochzeiger valley station (large free car parks available). By public transport: ÖBB to Imst-Pitztal railway station, from there take the regular VVT regional bus line 4204 directly to the stop Jerzens Hochzeiger Bergbahnen.

Tips

The gondola lift and the ZirbenPark circular trail at the middle station are designed to be accessible for wheelchairs and strollers; all-terrain pushchairs can be transported on the cable car free of charge. At the middle station, children receive wooden balls for the marble run, which they can keep as a souvenir. Be sure to also visit the Zeigerrestaurant with its panoramic terrace for traditional Tyrolean stone pine delicacies (Zirbenschmankerl).
